possible_splits.why: Bundles addition/subtraction of decimals with multiplication/division of decimals, which are taught in different grades and fail for different reasons.
Multi-step problems with all four operations across signed fractions AND decimals — really an umbrella over MS.QNT.6 and MS.QNT.7 applied in context.
Bundles naming lines/rays/parallel/perpendicular with classifying acute/right/obtuse angles — two different vocabularies.
Evaluating square and cube roots is a computational skill; classifying and approximating irrationals is a number-sense skill. Different failure modes.
Expanding and factoring are inverse operations students master at different times.
Rigid motions (congruence) and dilations (similarity) are two distinct big ideas crammed into one skill.
Bundles basic angle pairs, triangle angle sum, AND parallel-line transversals — three separate lessons.
Measures of center and measures of variability are separate competencies, and MAD in particular is its own thing.
GCF factoring and factoring by grouping are different techniques; grouping depends on GCF but is a separate hurdle.
Taking square roots and completing the square are bundled; the first is a quick method, the second a full procedure.
Difference of squares and perfect-square trinomials are two distinct patterns.
Conditional-statement forms (converse/inverse/contrapositive) and biconditionals are separate logic ideas from writing conditionals.
Composing transformations and identifying symmetry are related but taught and assessed separately.
Pyramids/cones and spheres use unrelated formulas; also bundles surface area with volume, four formula families in one skill.
Cross-sections, solids of revolution, and Cavalieri's principle are three separate ideas.
Remainder theorem (evaluation) and factor theorem (divisibility) are distinct uses.
Simplifying rational expressions and multiplying/dividing them are separate steps students confuse.
Common-base method and the logarithm method are different strategies with different prerequisites.
Arithmetic series, finite geometric series, and infinite convergent series each need their own formula and reasoning about convergence.
Same bundling as ALG2.EQV.8+9 combined into one PREC skill: division technique plus two theorems.
Matrix addition/scaling is trivial; matrix multiplication with dimension rules is the real skill.
Plotting polar points and converting equations between polar and rectangular are quite different in difficulty.
Tangent/cotangent graphs and the reciprocal secant/cosecant graphs are built from different reasoning.
Displacement and total distance traveled are the classic confusion pair; separating them would let the tutor target the absolute-value step.
